issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address never asserts the verify_signature response is valid
issues.detail: The new test calls verify_signature(...) but discards the return value. Because verify_signature returns VerifySignatureResponse(isValid=False, error=...) instead of raising on failure, the test silently passes even if signing/verification regresses. Add assert response.isValid is True to make the round-trip assertion meaningful.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring still references the obsolete `request` parameter
issues.detail: The function was extracted from the RPC method and now takes individual keyword args (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address), but the docstring still says `:param request:` / `:return:`. Update or remove the stale docstring so the new util's API is documented correctly.

issues.description: Module-level signing_mode_enum helper shadows a property of the same name on request dataclasses
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py defines a free function signing_mode_enum(request) and also adds signing_mode_enum properties on VerifySignature/SignMessageByAddress/SignMessageByID that delegate to it. The shared name creates a namespace collision, hurts navigation, and risks import-ergonomic bugs. Rename the helper (e.g. _signing_mode_from_flags) or inline it.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is an instance method on Wallet but uses no instance state
issues.detail: It is defined on Wallet yet always invoked through main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(...) even when signing for DID/NFT wallets, and never references self. Make it a @staticmethod or move it to signing.py so DID/NFT signing paths do not have to reach across an unrelated wallet instance for a pure function.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum relies on implicit fallthrough for the default CHIP_0002 case
issues.detail: The helper covers three explicit if/elif branches and falls through to CHIP_0002 for the remaining (not is_hex, safe_mode) case. The truth-table is exhaustive today but the implicit fallthrough is hard to audit and fragile to future edits. Make the final case an explicit elif and/or assert_never for unreachable inputs.

issues.description: Layering inversion: signing util imports VerifySignatureResponse from wallet_request_types
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py imports VerifySignatureResponse from chia.wallet.wallet_request_types, while RPC code imports the util. Putting a response DTO inside a low-level util that other wallet modules depend on creates a layering inversion and a future circular-import hazard. Consider relocating the DTO or constructing the response in the RPC layer.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a clean lift-and-shift refactor that consolidates duplicated sign/verify logic from Wallet/DIDWallet/NFTWallet into chia/wallet/util/signing.py, with no P0 correctness or security regressions and behavior preserved across all four signing modes. The dominant concerns are quality and hygiene: the new test_sign_message_by_address never asserts isValid so it cannot catch regressions, verify_signature carries a stale `:param request:` docstring, and the module-level signing_mode_enum helper shares a name with properties of the same name on the request dataclasses. Additionally, convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is an instance method that uses no instance state yet is reached through main_wallet for DID/NFT signing, and the signing_mode_enum helper relies on implicit fallthrough for the CHIP_0002 default case. A minor layering concern remains around the util importing a response DTO from wallet_request_types.
